- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 5–10 days), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to recent highs.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast peak at 1–2% above recent high.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-period, model fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per negative sentiment day.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting trends after strong rallies; add 0.5–1.0% lagged mean reversion adjustment if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days show strong downward momentum, model often misses the bottom; add 1–2% downward bias to early forecast days.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model overconfidently holds high; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per positive sentiment day.
